name: High Power Aristocrats Edgar Markov; Guide at the bottom
description:
{"ops":[{"insert":"I’ll try to keep this as compact and concise as possible to give you a quick overview of the overarching gameplan and winning lines of this deck.

"},{"attributes":{"underline":true,"bold":true},"insert":"General"},{"insert":"

Although you’re producing free vampire tokens you want to manage your resources and not waste them through mindless swinging for the face."},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"Chip in combat damage where you can but don’t overextend, it’s not the core strategy of this deck."},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"Don’t be afraid  to sacrifice creatures to draw into more efficient things or combo pieces to close out the game."},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"Prepare to become the archenemy"},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"
"},{"attributes":{"underline":true,"bold":true},"insert":"Mulligan"},{"insert":"

You’ll want to have at least two lands in hand with at least one piece of card draw, the latter is mandatory to dig through your deck to find more draw / combo pieces.
Cherries on top for a rocket fueled start, in no particular order:
A vampire one drop"},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"Bloodchief Ascension (Drop it on Turn 1,2 or even 3 and enjoy the constant life gain, ridiculous things happen once the board gets wiped. If not removed this card can win grindy games on it's own)"},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"Vampiric tutor – for obvious reasons, although boring"},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"Impact tremors"},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"Any kind of sac outlet"},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"
"},{"attributes":{"underline":true,"bold":true},"insert":"Strategy"},{"insert":"

Emphasizing this again as there’s this huge missconception that every Edgar Deck is an aggro deck:  don’t overextend and protect your creatures as they’re your main ressource to make an aristocrats strategy work.
You don’t have to run away with the game through huge swings, although this can happen, the more common path to close out a game is playing defensively and slowly assembling your win.
"},{"attributes":{"italic":true,"bold":true},"insert":"Early on it is important to control the board and slow your enemy down while gaining some life"},{"insert":". Cards like Dictate of Erebos, Gravepact, Contamination, Authority of the Consuls and especially Priest of the forgotten Gods (which is multi-tool really) will help you with that and should buy you enough time to develope your game state and eventually draw into Wincons.

"},{"attributes":{"underline":true,"bold":true},"insert":"Closing out the game"},{"insert":"

So there’s quite a few paths that lead to victory and explosively so:

Bolas Citadel in combination with Necropotence allows you to dig through your deck, while not getting blocked by already having played a land. You can just exile the unplayable land from top of your 		    library and keep digging."},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"Bolas citadel and Ayara or Impact Tremors like effects combined with dropping a lot of vampires will usually be enough to ping down your opponents."},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"Having a big enough board of vampires and dropping a Malakir Bloodwitch is not too unusual either (can happen with or without a Bolas Citadel out)."},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"Bloodthirsty Conqueror and Vito , Thorn of the Duskrose go straight up infinite with each other if you gain life or deal any kind of damage to an opponent."},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"Bloodchief Ascnesion combined with a boardwipe can be devastating for your enemies."},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"Unlocking Funeral Room into the Awakening Hall can be a winning move with other pieces already on the board such as, you guessed it, Impact Tremor-kind of effects."},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"Phyrexian Altar, Oathsworn Vampire and any kind of lifegain / drain effect will enable you to sacrifice Oathsword Vampire and a Vampire Token over and over for near unlimited etb / death triggers."},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"Inkshield on it’s own is already a strong tool not to only avoid combat damage but to maybe even win a game with Impact Tremors or similar kind of effects out."},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"Blood for the Blood God! Can also be used as a finishing tool, although 8 damage on it’s own is most of the time not enough (feel free to use to refill your hand instead if required)."},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"Last but not least Bloodletter of Aclazotz supports most of the above winning lines but is on it’s own already pretty strong and can enable wins through combat damage."},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"
"},{"attributes":{"underline":true,"bold":true},"insert":"Pushing things further"},{"insert":"

If you wanted to tune things even tighter you could include more tutor effects to make things more consistent, this should catapult you into fringe cEDH territory (although I can't really vouch for that as I haven't tried it yet).

"}]}
